title: Sparse trace bucketing for low-cost long-tail capture and replay
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Reduce tracing hotpath overhead while preserving the ability to analyze long-tail perf regressions. The ticket implements a lightweight, sparse bucketing layer in the hotpath that emits tiny fingerprints and metadata to the trace pipeline; a background rehydration service expands selected buckets into full spans for storage and developer analysis. Goals: 1) reduce per-request allocations and CPU on the hotpath, 2) keep tail signal fidelity for posthoc replay and debugging, 3) enable policy-driven selection (SLO breaches, anomaly signals, customer-impact). This approach complements existing probabilistic adaptive samplers by providing deterministic bucket-level retention for critical outliers.
background: Current samplers are probabilistic and adapt to QPS, but we still see noise in tail investigations: either low sample rate for a tenant makes root-cause attribution hard, or enabling higher sample rates increases hotpath CPU and memory allocations. Previous work focused on prefilters and deferred commits; this design trades slightly more pipeline complexity for much lower hotpath cost by emitting compact tokens instead of full spans on every request.
proposed_solution: 1) Hotpath: compute 64-bit lightweight fingerprint + 8-bit reason flags + 16-bit route bucket id and emit as a compact trace token in place of full span when sampling policy indicates 'sparse-bucketize'. Implementation uses zero-allocation xorshift64 PRNG + preallocated byte buffers to avoid temporary objects. 2) Streaming: tokens flow to a new bucketing topic in the trace pipeline. 3) Background rehydrator: periodically replays sampled tokens against a short-lived context cache to assemble full spans by fetching deferred metadata (request headers, exemplar slices) from a short retention fast-store, or by requesting the agent to emit a retrospective span via sidechannel. 4) Controller: SLO-driven rules decide which buckets to expand (e.g., high error-rate bucket, high-latency percentile, tenant-specific thresholds). 5) Fall-back: if rehydration fails, token-level aggregates remain available for alerting and basic diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath token emission path increases p99 serving latency by <0.2ms for 95% of requests and adds <3% CPU at 99th percentile under current load profile
End-to-end increase in trace pipeline ingress size <= 10% compared to baseline (when sparse-bucketize is enabled globally)
Rehydrator restores full spans for >=90% of selected buckets within 30s of selection under normal load
Runbooks exist for enabling/disabling sparse-bucketize per-tenant and for forcing immediate rehydration
E2E tests cover token->bucket->rehydration flow; benchmarks show allocation reductions on hotpath compared to current sampled-span emission
rollout_plan: 1. Implement hotpath token emitter behind feature flag and compile-time config to ensure zero impact if disabled
2. Add telemetry counters: tokens_emitted_total, token_emit_latency_ms, token_emit_alloc_bytes, rehydration_success_total, rehydration_latency_ms
3. Run shadow mode: emit tokens to bucketing topic while still sending full spans; collect performance delta for 2 weeks
4. Enable sparse-bucketize for a small set of low-risk internal tenants, monitor CPU and p99 latency for 72 hours
5. Progressive ramp: expand to non-critical customers, then to all customers with auto-disable thresholds if pipeline pressure exceeds limits
6. Post-rollout: retire redundant prefilter paths and update docs and runbooks
metrics_and_observability: End-user impact: per-tenant trace-coverage and trace-resolution (percent of incidents with full-span for top-10 alerts)
SLO guard: if rehydration_success_rate < 0.85 for 15m, auto-disable sparse-bucketize for affected tenant
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Rehydration may fail under heavy load -> Mitigation: graceful fallback to token-only diagnostics + automatic disable if failure rate high
Risk: Added pipeline topic increases storage/ingest costs -> Mitigation: enable retention rollups and TTL for tokens, compress 64-bit fingerprint batches
Risk: Privacy/regulatory concerns with deferred metadata -> Mitigation: encrypt deferred stores with KMS and support opt-out per-tenant in Private deployments
Risk: Implementation bugs could cause token corruption -> Mitigation: add checksums and strict schema validation in pipeline consumer
dependencies: ENG-21011 (ingress routing improvements) - for efficient topic routing
ENG-31820 (async span encoding) - reuse async writer primitives for rehydrator write-back
security-review: must coordinate with Security & Compliance for deferred metadata storage
